title: Starbucks Taiwan's New 'Less Ice' Fee Angers Coffee Drinkers
summaryZh: 星巴克少冰補滿收15元，消費者反彈
summaryHi: स्टारबक्स ताइवान ने कम बर्फ़ वाले पेय को भरने पर NT$15 शुल्क लगाया, ग्राहक नाराज़।
summaryEs: Starbucks Taiwán cobra NT$15 por rellenar bebidas sin hielo y los clientes protestan.
summaryJa: スターバックス台湾が氷少なめの補充に15元を課金し、客が反発。
summaryKo: 스타벅스 대만이 얼음 적게 주문 시 음료 보충에 NT$15를 받자 고객들이 반발했다.
summaryEn: Starbucks Taiwan now charges NT$15 to top up drinks ordered with less ice, and many customers are unhappy.
paragraphs: Starbucks Taiwan is facing a wave of criticism after introducing an extra NT$15 (about US$0.50) charge for customers who order iced drinks with less or no ice and want the cup topped up with milk or another liquid. The fee took effect on October 12; until then, the top-up had been free.

Unhappy customers quickly turned to social media, posting photos of "no ice" drinks that appeared only half full unless the extra money was paid. The posts attracted tens of thousands of reactions, and many people flooded the company's Facebook page demanding a return to the old policy. One user on Threads complained that the chain charges premium prices yet is "so stingy."

Cheng Kuei-i, an assistant professor of business at Chinese Culture University, said firms usually set prices according to cost, while customers judge them by the value they receive. The key issue, he argued, is whether people view the fee as paying for an extra option or as losing a service they had come to expect. He noted that EVA Airways kept its seat-selection fee despite complaints, while the Japanese chain Yayoi dropped a charge for rice refills.

Consultant Louis Lin said the charge could improve profit margins without raising base prices. Starbucks Taiwan, which now has more than 600 stores, has seen its operating margin fall from about 7.6% in 2018 to 6.3% in 2023. The company did not respond to requests for comment.
Starbucks has more than 600 coffee shops in Taiwan. Many people there like cold drinks with ice. Some people ask for less ice or no ice.
Before, the shop filled the cup to the top for free. But since October 12, people must pay 15 Taiwan dollars more for this. That is about 50 US cents.
Many customers are angry. They put photos on the internet. The photos show cold drinks with no ice. The cups look half empty. One person said, "How can they expect people to buy coffee like this?"
A teacher at a university says people do not think about cost. They think about value. If they feel they are losing something, they get upset.
Starbucks did not answer questions from reporters.

Starbucks Taiwan has started charging customers an extra NT$15, about US$0.50, if they order an iced drink with less ice or no ice and want the cup filled to the top with milk or another drink. The new fee began on October 12. Before that, topping up the cup was free.

The change has made many customers unhappy. People shared photos on social media of iced drinks ordered without ice that looked only half full. These posts received tens of thousands of comments, and many people asked the company on Facebook to bring back the old rule.
Some customers found clever ways around the fee. One person suggested bringing your own cup with ice already inside and ordering a hot drink. Customers who bring a reusable cup also get NT$10 off.

Cheng Kuei-i, a business teacher at Chinese Culture University, said companies set prices by cost, but customers judge them by value. The question is whether people see the fee as a new option or as losing something they used to get.
A business adviser said the fee helps the company earn more without raising drink prices. Starbucks has not commented.

Starbucks Taiwan is facing a wave of criticism after introducing an extra NT$15 (about US$0.50) charge for customers who order iced drinks with less or no ice and want the cup topped up with milk or another liquid. The fee took effect on October 12; until then, the top-up had been free.

Unhappy customers quickly turned to social media, posting photos of "no ice" drinks that appeared only half full unless the extra money was paid. The posts attracted tens of thousands of reactions, and many people flooded the company's Facebook page demanding a return to the old policy. One user on Threads complained that the chain charges premium prices yet is "so stingy."

Cheng Kuei-i, an assistant professor of business at Chinese Culture University, said firms usually set prices according to cost, while customers judge them by the value they receive. The key issue, he argued, is whether people view the fee as paying for an extra option or as losing a service they had come to expect. He noted that EVA Airways kept its seat-selection fee despite complaints, while the Japanese chain Yayoi dropped a charge for rice refills.

Consultant Louis Lin said the charge could improve profit margins without raising base prices. Starbucks Taiwan, which now has more than 600 stores, has seen its operating margin fall from about 7.6% in 2018 to 6.3% in 2023. The company did not respond to requests for comment.

A seemingly trivial NT$15 charge has sparked an outsized backlash against Starbucks Taiwan. Since October 12, customers who order iced drinks with reduced or no ice and want their cup topped up with milk or another liquid have had to pay the extra fee, roughly US$0.50, for a service that was previously free.

The reaction online was swift. Customers posted images of "ice-free" drinks that looked conspicuously half full unless the surcharge was paid, and the posts drew tens of thousands of responses. The company's Facebook page was flooded with demands to reinstate the old policy, while some users shared workarounds, such as filling a reusable cup with ice and ordering a hot drink, which also earns a NT$10 discount.

Cheng Kuei-i, an assistant professor at Chinese Culture University, framed the dispute as a question of perception. Businesses tend to price according to cost, he said, but consumers judge prices by perceived value. Whether the fee survives depends on whether customers regard it as an optional extra or as the withdrawal of a service they had come to take for granted. He pointed to EVA Airways, which kept a seat-selection fee despite early anger, and the restaurant chain Yayoi, which abandoned charging for rice refills.

Consultant Louis Lin noted that the fee lifts margins without touching headline prices, a tempting option for a chain whose operating margin slipped from about 7.6% in 2018 to 6.3% in 2023 as labour, rent and utility costs rose. Starbucks Taiwan has not commented.

Few pricing decisions provoke as much anger as removing something customers once received free, as Starbucks Taiwan is discovering. Since October 12, the chain has imposed a NT$15 (approximately US$0.50) surcharge on customers who request less or no ice in a cold drink and expect the cup to be topped up with milk or another liquid.

The backlash has been considerable. Photographs of seemingly half-empty "no ice" beverages circulated widely on social media, generating tens of thousands of comments, and the company's Facebook page was inundated with calls to restore the previous arrangement.

According to Cheng Kuei-i, an assistant professor of business at Chinese Culture University, the controversy illustrates the gap between how companies and consumers evaluate prices. Firms typically calculate prices on the basis of cost, whereas customers assess them in terms of perceived value. Crucially, a charge is far more likely to be tolerated if it is seen as payment for an additional option rather than the loss of an established entitlement. Cheng contrasted EVA Airways, which retained a contested seat-selection fee, with Yayoi, which withdrew a charge for rice refills.

From a commercial perspective, consultant Louis Lin observed that the surcharge improves profitability without raising base prices. This matters for a chain of more than 600 stores whose operating margin declined from roughly 7.6% in 2018 to 6.3% in 2023 amid rising labour, rent and utility costs.
Whether customers eventually accept the fee, or whether public pressure forces a reversal, remains to be seen. Starbucks Taiwan has so far declined to comment.

note.meaning: 激起；引發（負面反應）。文中指取消免費服務最易激起怒氣。
note.usage: provoke anger/a reaction/criticism；受詞多為負面情緒。

example.en: The decision provoked anger among parents.
example.zh: 這項決定激起了家長的憤怒。

noteEn.meaning: to cause a strong, often negative, reaction.

noteHi.meaning: तीव्र, अक्सर नकारात्मक, प्रतिक्रिया पैदा करना।
noteHi.exampleTr: इस फ़ैसले से अभिभावकों में ग़ुस्सा भड़का।

noteEs.meaning: causar una reacción fuerte, a menudo negativa.
noteEs.exampleTr: La decisión provocó la ira de los padres.

noteJa.meaning: （否定的な）反応を引き起こす。
noteJa.exampleTr: その決定は保護者の怒りを招いた。

public.ex: The park is open to the public.

put.en: to place something somewhere, also online
put.ex: He put the video on the internet.

question.en: something you ask to get an answer
question.ex: The teacher asked a difficult question.

raising.en: making something higher, such as a price
raising.ex: The shop is raising its prices again.

rather.ex: I'd like tea rather than coffee.

reaction.en: what people say or do in response
reaction.ex: The reaction to the news was angry.

reactions.en: responses such as likes or comments online
reactions.ex: The post got thousands of reactions.

reduced.ex: The shop reduced its prices this week.

refills.en: second servings of a drink or food

regard.en: think about in a particular way
regard.ex: Many regard her as the best player.

reinstate.en: to bring back something that was removed
reinstate.ex: Fans want the club to reinstate the old logo.

note.meaning: 恢復（原狀）。文中指顧客要求恢復舊政策。
note.usage: reinstate a policy/rule/sb；比 restore 更正式，常用於制度或職位。

example.en: The council agreed to reinstate the free bus service.
example.zh: 議會同意恢復免費公車服務。

noteEn.meaning: to bring back a rule, service or person to a former position.
noteEn.usage: 'reinstate a policy'; more formal than 'bring back'.

noteHi.meaning: किसी नियम या सेवा को फिर से लागू करना।
noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने मुफ़्त बस सेवा बहाल करने पर सहमति दी।

noteEs.meaning: volver a poner en vigor una norma o servicio.
noteEs.usage: reinstate a policy; más formal que bring back.
noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento aceptó restablecer el autobús gratuito.

noteJa.meaning: 規則や制度を元に戻す。
noteJa.usage: reinstate a policy；bring back より改まった表現。
noteJa.exampleTr: 議会は無料バスの復活に同意した。

noteKo.usage: reinstate a policy; bring back보다 격식 있다.
noteKo.exampleTr: 의회는 무료 버스 서비스를 복원하기로 했다.

remains.ex: The shop remains open until late.

rent.en: to pay money to live in a place
rent.ex: Many students rent a room near college.

request.ex: The council agreed to our request.

requests.en: polite or formal asks for something
requests.ex: The office ignored our requests for help.

respond.ex: How will the minister respond to the report?

restaurant.en: a place where you buy and eat meals
restaurant.ex: We ate at a seafood restaurant.

restore.en: to bring back something that existed before
restore.ex: They plan to restore the old theatre.

retained.en: kept something instead of losing or removing it
retained.ex: The team retained its best players.

return.en: going back to an earlier state
return.ex: The return to winter time brings dark evenings.

reusable.en: able to be used again and again
reusable.ex: Take a reusable bag to the market.

reversal.en: a change to the opposite decision
reversal.ex: Protests led to a reversal of the plan.

rice.en: small white grains cooked and eaten as food
rice.ex: We had fish and rice for dinner.

rule.ex: There is an important rule to remember.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

seat-selection.ex: Some airlines charge a seat-selection fee.

see.ex: Let's see if the shop is open.

seemingly.ex: It was a seemingly simple question.

seen.ex: The bird was seen near the lake.

service.en: something a business does for its customers
service.ex: The café offers a free refill service.

set.en: to decide a price or level
set.ex: The shop sets its prices every month.

shared.en: gave others something to see or use

shop.en: a place where you buy things
shop.ex: Her family runs a gift shop.

shops.ex: The local shop closes at nine.

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

social.en: relating to people sharing online (social media)
social.ex: Many teens spend hours on social media.

some.en: a number of, but not all

something.en: a thing that is not named

stingy.en: not willing to give or spend money
stingy.ex: He is too stingy to buy a round of drinks.

suggested.en: gave an idea for others to think about
suggested.ex: My friend suggested a new café.

surcharge.en: an extra amount added to the normal price
surcharge.ex: There is a surcharge for late payment.

note.meaning: 附加費。文中指少冰補滿要多付的15元。
note.usage: impose/add a surcharge on sth；比 fee 更強調「在原價之上額外加收」。

example.en: Airlines added a fuel surcharge to every ticket.
example.zh: 航空公司在每張機票上加收燃油附加費。

noteEn.meaning: an extra amount added to the usual price.
noteEn.usage: 'impose a surcharge on sth'; stresses an amount on top of the normal price.

noteHi.meaning: सामान्य कीमत पर जोड़ा गया अतिरिक्त शुल्क।
noteHi.exampleTr: एयरलाइनों ने हर टिकट पर ईंधन अधिभार जोड़ा।

noteEs.exampleTr: Las aerolíneas añadieron un recargo por combustible a cada billete.

noteJa.meaning: 通常価格に上乗せされる追加料金。
noteJa.usage: impose a surcharge on 〜 の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: 航空会社は全航空券に燃油サーチャージを加えた。

noteKo.usage: impose a surcharge on ~ 형태로 쓴다.
noteKo.exampleTr: 항공사들은 모든 항공권에 유류 할증료를 붙였다.

survives.ex: Only one old shop survives on the street.

swift.ex: The shop gave a swift reply to my complaint.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

take.zh: 視為（take for granted：視為理所當然）
take.en: (take for granted) expect without thinking about it
take.ex: Never take good health for granted.

teacher.ex: The teacher read us a story.

tend.ex: Cats tend to sleep during the day.

tens.ex: Tens of thousands joined the march.

terms.ex: Both sides agreed on the terms of the deal.

then.ex: First read the text, then answer the questions.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

think.ex: Experts think a deal is possible.

thousands.en: many thousands; a very large number
thousands.ex: Thousands of birds fly south each year.

tolerated.ex: Noise after midnight will not be tolerated.

note.meaning: 被容忍。文中指收費若被視為額外選項較易被接受。
note.usage: be tolerated；tolerate + n./V-ing；比 accept 更帶「勉強忍受」之意。

example.en: Late arrivals will not be tolerated.

noteEn.meaning: accepted even though it is not liked.
noteEn.usage: 'be tolerated'; weaker than 'welcomed', means reluctantly accepted.

noteHi.meaning: नापसंद होने पर भी स्वीकार किया जाना।
noteHi.exampleTr: देर से आना बर्दाश्त नहीं किया जाएगा।

noteJa.meaning: 好ましくないが受け入れられる。

took.ex: She took first place in the race.

top.ja: 上端（to the top：いっぱいに）
top.en: the highest part; (to the top) completely full
top.ex: Fill the glass to the top.

top-up.en: an extra amount added to fill something
top-up.ex: The top-up used to be free.

topped.en: (topped up) filled to the top with more liquid
topped.ex: The waiter topped up our glasses.

topping.en: (topping up) filling to the top with more liquid
topping.ex: Topping up your phone credit is easy.

touching.ex: They cut costs without touching wages.

trivial.ex: The cost is far from trivial.

turned.en: went to something for help or a way to act
turned.ex: Many fans turned to the internet for news.

typically.ex: Trains are typically late in winter.

university.ex: She wants to study law at university.

up.en: used with 'top' to mean fill completely

upset.ex: She was upset about the new rule.

used.en: put into service for a purpose
used.ex: The old bricks were used again.

user.en: a person who uses a product
user.ex: Every road user must be careful.

users.ex: All road users should slow down.

utility.en: basic services such as power and water
utility.ex: Utility bills rose sharply this winter.

value.es: valor (value for money: buena relación calidad-precio)
value.ex: This phone is good value for money.
value.hi: मूल्य (value for money पैसे का सही उपयोग)
value.ja: 価値（value for money 費用対効果）
value.ko: 가치 (value for money 비용 대비 가치)
value.zh: 價值（value for money 物有所值）

view.en: to think about something in a certain way
view.ex: Many people view the plan as unfair.

want.en: to wish to have or do

wave.ex: A second wave of strikes is planned.

ways.ex: There are many ways to save energy.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

widely.ex: Opinions on the plan differ widely.

withdrawal.en: the act of taking something away
withdrawal.ex: There was a withdrawal of support.

withdrew.ex: The unions withdrew from the talks.

workarounds.en: clever ways of avoiding a problem
workarounds.ex: Users quickly found workarounds for the bug.

yet.ex: The cost is not yet known.
